review.notes: Built on the course: Conceptual Framework, IAS 1 features and current/non-current, IAS 7 classification, IFRS 15 five steps, allocation by SSP, point in time vs over time, IAS 2 cost and NRV, IAS 16 cost and depreciation, IFRS 16 lessee model. Calculations checked. Fictional company.

content.company: Meridian Equipment (fictional), selling and servicing industrial machines
content.briefing: It is year-end. You prepare the IFRS financial statements for the auditors. Several transactions need judgement: a bundled sale, stock that lost value, a new machine, a lease and the cash flow statement.

variants.text: A bank loan is repayable in 8 months. Where does it go in the statement of financial position?

choices.f: Due within 12 months, so current.
Only liabilities due after 12 months are non-current.
A loan is an obligation, not equity.

variants.text: A customer owes Kz 5 m, and you owe the same customer Kz 2 m. The CFO wants to show Kz 3 m net.

choices.t: Show both, unless offsetting is allowed
choices.f: No offsetting unless a standard requires or permits it.

choices.t: Show Kz 3 m net; it is simpler
choices.f: Offsetting hides the gross positions.

choices.t: Show only the Kz 5 m receivable
choices.f: The payable must also be reported.

variants.text: The company has lost money for 3 years and its main loan is in default. Which assumption must management assess?

choices.f: Material uncertainty must be disclosed, or another basis used.
Materiality is about what matters to users, not survival.
An enhancing characteristic, not the issue here.

variants.text: Paying interest on a loan: in which cash flow section under IAS 7?

choices.f: IAS 7 allows a choice, applied consistently.
Investing is for long-term assets and investments.

choices.t: It is not a cash flow at all
choices.f: Interest paid is a cash outflow.

variants.text: You sell a machine plus one year of servicing for Kz 1,000 k. Stand-alone prices: machine Kz 900 k, service Kz 300 k. How much is allocated to the machine?

choices.f: 1,000 x 900 / 1,200. The discount is shared across both.
That gives the whole discount to the service.
That gives the whole discount to the machine.

variants.text: In the same deal, when is the service revenue recognised?

choices.t: Over the year, as service is given
choices.f: The customer consumes the benefit as you perform.
Nothing is delivered yet at signing.

choices.t: At the end of the year
choices.f: The service is delivered across the year.

variants.text: What is step 2 of the IFRS 15 five-step model?

choices.f: Contract, obligations, price, allocation, recognition.
That is step 3.
That is step 5.

variants.text: A customer earns a 5% rebate if it buys over Kz 50 m this year. It will very likely qualify. How do you treat it?

choices.f: Reduce revenue for the expected rebate.

choices.t: Ignore it until the year ends
choices.f: Revenue would be overstated during the year.

choices.t: Book it as an expense later
choices.f: Rebates reduce revenue, not expenses.

variants.text: Imported spare parts: price Kz 100 k, non-recoverable duty Kz 10 k, inbound transport Kz 5 k, selling commission Kz 3 k. Inventory cost?

choices.f: Price + duty + transport in. Selling costs are excluded.
Selling costs are not part of inventory cost.
Duty and inbound transport are part of cost.

variants.text: A part cost Kz 50 k. It can now sell for Kz 60 k, with Kz 15 k of costs to sell. At what value is it carried?

choices.f: Lower of cost (50) and NRV (60 - 15 = 45).
NRV is below cost, so write it down.
Selling price before costs is not NRV.

variants.text: New machine: price Kz 800 k, delivery Kz 30 k, installation Kz 20 k, staff training Kz 15 k. Initial cost under IAS 16?

choices.f: Training is expensed, not capitalised.
Training is not part of the asset's cost.
Delivery and installation are included.

variants.text: Machine cost Kz 1,000 k, residual value Kz 100 k, useful life 5 years, straight line. Annual depreciation?

choices.f: You ignored the residual value.
Residual value is subtracted, not added.

variants.text: General admin costs for the head office are part of inventory cost, says a colleague. Correct?

choices.f: IAS 2 excludes selling and general admin costs.

choices.t: Yes: all costs belong to inventory
choices.f: Only costs to bring stock to its location and condition.
Size does not change the rule.

variants.text: Some stock was spoiled by abnormal flooding in the warehouse. How do you treat the loss?

choices.t: Expense it; abnormal waste is excluded
choices.f: Abnormal waste is not part of inventory cost.

choices.t: Add it to the cost of remaining stock
choices.f: That overstates inventory.
Losses are recognised when they occur.

variants.text: You lease a warehouse for 5 years. Under IFRS 16, what do you recognise at the start?

choices.t: A right-of-use asset and a lease liability
choices.f: The liability is the present value of lease payments.
That was the old operating-lease approach for lessees.

choices.t: The full building as owned PPE
choices.f: You control its use, not the building itself.

variants.text: How is the lease liability measured at commencement?

choices.t: Present value of the lease payments
choices.f: Discounted at the rate in the lease or your borrowing rate.

choices.t: Total of all payments, not discounted
choices.f: IFRS 16 uses present value.
The liability is about payments, not the building.

variants.text: Your indirect cash flow statement starts from profit. Depreciation was Kz 180 k. What do you do with it?

choices.t: Add it back: it is non-cash
choices.f: Depreciation reduced profit without using cash.
That double-counts a non-cash cost.
It must be adjusted to reach cash.

variants.text: You bought the new machine for cash. Which section of the cash flow statement?

choices.f: Long-term asset purchases are investing.
Operating covers trading cash flows.
Financing is about loans and equity.

variants.text: From which date does IFRS 18 replace IAS 1?

choices.f: New categories and subtotals in profit or loss.
Too early.
It has a set effective date.

variants.text: Closing cash in the cash flow statement does not match the balance sheet. What do you check first?

choices.f: Closing cash must equal the balance sheet cash.
The statements must reconcile exactly.

choices.t: Change the balance sheet to match
choices.f: Forcing a match hides the error.
